content: Before taking ritonavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Ritonavir can cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) may exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, be aware that this medication may increase your blood sugar levels. Regularly monitor your blood sugar as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Ritonavir treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. However, this medication does pass into breast milk, so discuss breastfeeding with your doctor. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Ritonavir interacts with many medications, potentially slowing down or speeding up their removal from your body, which may affect their efficacy. Similarly, other medications can influence how ritonavir is metabolized, impacting its effectiveness. Examples of interacting drugs include apalutamide and rifampin. Ritonavir may also reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods like pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Consult your doctor or pharmacist about using reliable backup birth control methods while on this medication. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking ritonavir, it is essential to undergo regular lab and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load measurements, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol levels, and blood sugar monitoring. Keep all scheduled medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store ritonavir capsules in the refrigerator, away from light, and do not freeze them. Capsules may also be stored at room temperature if necessary, but discard them after 30 days if kept at room temperature. Store tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture, and avoid storing them in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused medication. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about ritonavir. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
